components.css: .ds-units{display:inline-flex;gap:3px;padding:3px;border-radius:48px;background:var(--tabs-bar-bg)}.ds-units button{font-family:"DM Sans",sans-serif;height:30px;padding:4px 12px;border:0;border-radius:48px;background:transparent;color:var(--tabs-text-muted);font-size:12px;cursor:pointer;transition:color var(--tabs-dur) var(--tabs-ease)}.ds-units button[aria-pressed="true"]{background:var(--tabs-pill-bg);color:var(--tabs-text-active)}.ds-units button:hover{color:var(--tabs-text-active)}.ds-units button:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--blue);outline-offset:3px}@media(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-units button{transition:none}}

narrative.overview: An open, precise workspace for reading national wind forecasts and checking their evidence. White plotting space, graphite text and cool gray subdivisions keep the data prominent. Sparse copy identifies the decision, units and source limits.
keyCharacteristics: Compact horizontal navigation and rectangular controls.
Cobalt forecasts and amber retrospective observations.
One sans family with tabular numerals for measurement.

rules.name: The Series Identity Rule
rules.body: Keep forecast and error magnitude cobalt; keep actuals and signed bias amber. Legends and units identify the meaning of each series.

rules.name: The Numeric Alignment Rule
rules.body: Use tabular numerals for metric values and tables, and right-align quantitative table columns. Keep units next to the values or in the column heading.

rules.name: The Open Plot Rule
rules.body: Keep the plotting field on the white workspace. Use the adjacent tonal rail to collect measurements.

dos: **Do** preserve cobalt and amber series identities across charts and legends.
**Do** keep units, coverage and source limits readable beside the evidence.
**Do** use sparse labels and the shared DM Sans hierarchy.
**Do** preserve visible keyboard focus and reduced-motion behavior.
donts: **Don't** restore the green sidebar or Manrope display hierarchy.
**Don't** wrap open plots in decorative rounded cards.
**Don't** replace source gaps with visual certainty.
